name: CITEANCHOR-quote-min-halved
note: A quote shorter than the minimum names its line by a fragment a change elsewhere can repeat.

name: CITEANCHOR-edge-no-whitespace
note: Without the whitespace edge, a quote can only end at a bracket.

name: CITEANCHOR-edge-no-callee
note: A callee before its call is an edge (`export function seam`).

name: CITEANCHOR-edge-no-close
note: A closing bracket before what follows it is an edge.

name: CITEANCHOR-edge-inside-tokens
note: The old rule: a quote may end inside an operator or a path (`nothingText: () =`).

name: CITEANCHOR-balance-open-left
note: A quote that leaves a bracket open carried FOE1's scanner past its call.

name: CITEANCHOR-no-avoid
old: return (avoid != null ? quoteRun(fileText, lines, n, forbid, avoid, braces) : null) ?? quoteRun(fileText, lines, n, forbid, null, braces);
new: return quoteRun(fileText, lines, n, forbid, null, braces);
note: A quote of world.js written into exterior.js's comments was the first copy a test's indexOf met.

name: CITEANCHOR-standing-always-once
note: A quote that stands twice names no line.

name: CITEANCHOR-after-twin-ignored
old: if (afterText(lines[j - 1], line) === line) { if (j === n) return { quote: q, line }; break; }
new: if (afterText(lines[j - 1], line) === line && j === n) return { quote: q, line };
note: An after-form whose twin stands between names the twin.

name: CITEANCHOR-resolve-ambiguous-passes
note: A quote that stands twice resolves to its first copy, silently.

name: CITEANCHOR-no-mask
note: A file that cites its own line counts its quote twice, and the anchor stops resolving.

name: CITEANCHOR-row-takes-a-pipe
note: A `|` in a table row's quote splits the cell.

name: CITEANCHOR-span-not-carried
note: A span opened on the line above holds the cite; read per line, a `*` lands in prose.

name: CITEANCHOR-blank-keeps-span
note: A blank line ends a paragraph and any span in it.

name: CITEANCHOR-fence-not-code
old:
if (/^\s*```/.test(l)) { out.push(true); fence = !fence; open = false; continue; }
    if (fence) { out.push(true); continue; }
note: A fenced block is code.

name: CITEANCHOR-strike-unpaired-not-held
note: A strike opened on another line pairs wrongly with this one: the whole line is held.

name: CITEANCHOR-strike-whole-line
old: const struckAt = (col) => spans === null || spans.some(([a, b]) => col >= a && col < b);
note: The old rule: a closed Ledger row's live closing note held as a record.

name: CITEANCHOR-strike-ignored
old: const struckAt = (col) => spans === null || spans.some(([a, b]) => col >= a && col < b);
note: A struck record re-resolved - Port-Status's struck law broken.

name: CITEANCHOR-nudge-reach-one
old: for (let k = n + 1; k <= n + 3; k++) if (takes(k)) return { n: k, nudged: true };
new: for (let k = n + 1; k <= n + 1; k++) if (takes(k)) return { n: k, nudged: true };
note: A doc block's close names what it documents, a few lines on.

name: CITEANCHOR-chain-glued
old: if (before === false && it.sep.startsWith('/')) { push({ to: null, status: 'chain', file: r.file, n: it.n }); continue; }
note: A slash's continuation after a number left standing reads as that number's directory.

name: CITEANCHOR-settle-writes-null
old: const to = next == null ? a.text : m[1] + next;
note: A line its own cites leave unquotable writes `null` where the cite stood.

name: CITEANCHOR-launcher-not-foreign
note: The spec's retired launcher's numbers read as app/launcher/launcher.js's lines.

name: CITEANCHOR-relay-not-held
note: A relay file's cites rewritten: every byte there is a relay law (SLAM8).

name: CITEANCHOR-continuation-slash-is-root
note: A continuation's slash read as a root: `/world.js` resolves to nothing.

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-no-dfu
note: DFU named before a bare continuation no longer holds it ("DFU plays it first (:12)"): the C# line is anchored into our file.

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-no-csharp
note: C# named before a bare continuation no longer holds it.

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-no-pascal
note: A PascalCase name (StaticNPC.SetRuntimeData, MinDamage) before a bare continuation no longer holds it: DFU's line is anchored into our file, as Port-Ledger 815/817/927 were.

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-one-hump
note: Any capitalised word counts as a code name: a sentence that starts "The" holds the head's own continuation.

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-other-file-ignored
old: for (const m of between.matchAll(NAMED_FILE)) if (m[1] !== own) return false;
note: A file of ours named in prose no longer holds the continuation after it: verticalScrollBar.js's lines go to the head's file (Port-Ledger 702).

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-own-file-counts
note: The head's own file named again in its prose holds its own continuation.

name: CITEANCHOR-unclear-unwired
old: if (!headOwns(l.slice(from, it.col), r.file)) { push({ to: null, status: 'unclear', file: r.file, n: it.n }); continue; }   // a head's own slice is empty
note: The plan never asks whether the head owns its continuation: every C# line after one of ours is anchored into our file.

name: CITEANCHOR-after-no-indented-form
old: for (const line of raw === t ? [t] : [t, raw]) {
note: A close brace past its inner twin takes no after-form: the outer block's `  }` falls to the range's next line, as AUDIT REST II Q5's spawn tick did.

name: CITEANCHOR-after-always-trimmed
note: An indented after-form resolves trimmed: `.."  }"` names the inner twin's `    }`.

name: CITEANCHOR-brace-uncounted
old:
else if (braces && c === '{') brace++;
    else if (braces && c === '}' && --brace < 0) return false;
note: A comment's anchor carries a brace a scanner counts: BOOT-TDZ2 read `.."}"` in buildPixelNow's comment as the function's end.

name: CITEANCHOR-brace-close-first
note: A close before its open (`} else {`) dips a scanner's depth to the function's own level mid-body - the scan ends there.

name: CITEANCHOR-brace-open-left
note: A quote that leaves a `{` open (`if (x) {`) carries a scanner past the function's end.

name: CITEANCHOR-head-whole-with-brace
old: const whole = braces && !open && raw[end - 1] === '{' ? raw.slice(0, end - 1).trimEnd().length : end;
note: A block's head shorter than the minimum (`if (people) {`) is whole without its brace; without that it is nudged off its own line.

name: CITEANCHOR-opener-quote-balanced
note: The opener's quote must hold the brace its after-form's line closes, or the anchor is a lone `}` to a scanner.

name: CITEANCHOR-opener-any-indent
old: else if (l[c] === '{' && --depth === 0) return /^\s*/.exec(l)[0] === indent ? k : null;
note: A brace in a string miscounts the upward match: the opener found then stands at another indentation, and the anchor names another block's close.

name: CITEANCHOR-chain-not-walked
note: The close of an if/else chain whose last link (`} else {`) cannot be quoted takes no anchor, though the link before it can name it.

name: CITEANCHOR-closer-any-line
note: A line that leaves a brace open (`} else {`) is named after its opener - the anchor then leaves that brace open.

name: CITEANCHOR-head-not-nudged
note: A block's head whose only quote holds its brace (`_confirmExit() {`, whose name stands in its calls) is left a number, for a person, though its block's first line names it.

name: CITEANCHOR-opensblock-net
note: A line that closes one block and opens the next (`} else {`) opens a block too: its head is nudged like any other.

name: CITEANCHOR-takes-braces-free
old: quoteFor(text, lines, k, forbid, null, braces) != null
note: Whether a line takes an anchor is judged by the rule it will be written under: a head that only takes one with its brace is not passed over.

name: CITEANCHOR-braces-unwired-plan
note: The conversion writes a code comment's anchors with their braces unbalanced.

name: CITEANCHOR-braces-unwired-settle
note: The settle pass re-quotes a code comment's anchor with its braces unbalanced.

name: CITEANCHOR-braces-in-markdown
note: A Markdown doc's anchors lose the block heads and closes their braces would name.
